[[File:Metric lattice cube135.svg|thumb|Example valuation function on the cube lattice which makes it a metric lattice.]]
In the mathematical [[order theory|study of order]], a '''metric lattice''' {{mvar|L}} is a [[lattice (order)|lattice]] that admits a positive '''valuation''': a function {{math|''v'' ∈ ''L'' → {{mathbb|R}}}} satisfying, for any {{math|''a'', ''b'' ∈ ''L''}},<ref name=LatticeThry1>{{cite book | first = Daniel Edwin | last = Rutherford | year = 1965 | title = Introduction to Lattice Theory
|publisher = Oliver and Boyd|pages=20–22}}</ref> <math display=block>v(a)+v(b)=v(a\wedge b)+v(a\vee b)</math> and <math display=block>{a>b}\Rightarrow v(a)>v(b)\text{.}</math>

==Relation to other notions==
[[File:N5 abcde.svg|thumb|A lattice containing [[Modular lattice#Examples|N5]] (depicted) cannot be a metric one, since ''v''(''d'')+''v''(''c'') = ''v''(''e'')+''v''(''a'') = ''v''(''b'')+''v''(''c'') implies ''v''(''d'') = ''v''(''b''), contradicting ''v''(''d'') < ''v''(''b'').]]
A [[Boolean algebra]] is a metric lattice; any [[content (measure theory)|finitely-additive measure]] on its [[Stone's representation theorem for Boolean algebras|Stone dual]] gives a valuation.<ref name=LatticeThry2 />{{rp|252–254}}

Every metric lattice is a [[modular lattice]],<ref name=LatticeThry1 /> c.f. lower picture. It is also a [[metric space]], with distance function given by<ref name=FuzzyLogic /> <math display=block>d(x,y)=v(x\vee y)-v(x\wedge y)\text{.}</math>  With that metric, the [[join and meet]] are [[uniformly continuous]] [[contraction mapping|contractions]],<ref name=LatticeThry2>{{cite book|series=AMS Colloquium Publications 25|title=Lattice Theory|last=Birkhoff|first=Garrett|author-link=Garrett Birkhoff|edition=Revised|publisher=AMS|location=New York City|year=1948|hdl=2027/iau.31858027322886 |via=HathiTrust|url=https://hdl.handle.net/2027/iau.31858027322886}}</ref>{{rp|77}} and so extend to the metric [[completion (metric space)]].  That lattice is usually not the [[Dedekind-MacNeille completion]], but it is [[Conditionally complete lattice|conditionally complete]].<ref name=LatticeThry2 />{{rp|80}}

==Applications==
In the study of [[fuzzy logic]] and [[interval arithmetic]], the space of [[Continuous uniform distribution|uniform distribution]]s is a metric lattice.<ref name=FuzzyLogic>Kaburlasos, V. G. (2004). "FINs: Lattice Theoretic Tools for Improving Prediction of Sugar Production From Populations of Measurements." ''IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics, Part B (Cybernetics)'', 34(2), 1017–1030. [[doi:10.1109/tsmcb.2003.818558]]</ref>  Metric lattices are also key to von Neumann's construction of the [[continuous geometry|continuous projective geometry]].<ref name=LatticeThry2 />{{rp|126}}  A function satisfies the one-dimensional [[wave equation]] if and only if it is a valuation for the lattice of spacetime coordinates with the natural partial order.  A similar result should apply to any [[partial differential equation]] solvable by the [[method of characteristics]], but key features of the theory are lacking.<ref name=LatticeThry2 />{{rp|150–151}}
